items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I got to watch him in the late 50s... I was getting to know him a little bit

ctx.x: Yes. And it scared me off a little bit, but I wonder, what set you up to enjoy Cecil Taylor?

Cecil Taylor? Well first of all, when I first got into Cecil Taylor he was not quite the powerhouse he was at the time that he was a few years later. He was still finding his voice and he was playing in little coffee houses around Greenwich Village and on some pretty raggedy pianos, and I got to watch him in the late 50s, I got to watch him grow, which is always a wonderful thing to do with another artist, to watch them grow, watch them actually empower themselves. And so by the early 60s you could see the power…

Did you feel that his personality was reflected in his music that seemed to always be seeking the far boundaries? I may not be speaking exactly on point here but did he have a personality that reflected the way he played?
